payload.data_status: synthetic (generated for instrument exercise; no empirical content)
payload.label: demo_null
limitations: Counts on known-null data are recorded observations about the instrument, not a calibrated error rate.
The noise distribution is a chosen generator, not a model of any real measurement process.
No verdict is assigned about whether any count is acceptable.

recorded_summary.summary_basis: recorded counts over synthetic replications; no significance assigned

limitations: Appearance across thresholds is recorded, not characterized as stability or instability.
The threshold ladder is analyst-chosen; the record does not judge the choice.
payload.ordering_rule: thresholds and cases used in given order; never sorted

limitations: Appearance across permutations is recorded, not characterized as robustness or fragility.
A permuted order is a different input to the engine, not an error; the engine's no-sorting contract still holds per scan.

coincidence_record.note: Coincidence of candidate regions across factors is recorded only; it does not establish a shared cause, a confound, or its absence.

limitations: Each factor is scanned independently; joint factor structure is not modeled.
A region appearing under only one factor is recorded, not explained.

payload.description: Four instrument-level experiments were run on synthetic data and recorded without interpretation.
evidence: null_baseline: 11 max candidate region(s) over 25 noise replications
coupling: 2 coincident pair(s) across two factors
proposed_next_tests: repeat each procedure on held-out synthetic generators
run the same procedures on a documented real dataset
unresolved_questions: Do candidate-region counts on real data differ from the null record?
Which regions persist across thresholds, and does persistence matter here?
Does scan order affect regions on real, unordered case sets?
Do coincident regions across factors indicate a confound?
